sentences.text: The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondent with regard to the death of deceased Narayanappa in the road traffic accident that took place on 26-09-2022.

2. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 26-09-2022 at about 6.20 p.m., when the petitioner was pedestrian by side of the road, proceeding on near Chowdeshwari temple, Kannamangala main road,
Bangalore district, at that time, a water tanker bearing Reg.No. KA-51-A-8675 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, without following any traffic rules, came at high speed and dashed to the petitioner and caused accident.
Due to the impact, the petitioner was fell down and sustained several injuries on vital parts of the body.
Immediately, injured was shifted to Sai Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and shifted to MTB hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and undergone surgery.
The petitioner has spent an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges.

It is further submitted that due to the injuries sustained in the accident he was completely bed ridden, cannot run, jump, cannot lift or carry any weight, unable to sleep properly and he cannot do his activities as earlier to the accident.

At the time of accident he was aged about 90 years doing coolie work and earning a sum of Rs.1,000/- per day and due to the injuries he lost his earning capacity and facing great financial difficulties.

sentences.text: It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Water Tanker bearing Reg. No.KA-51-A-8675 for which the Whitefield traffic police has registered a case in Cr No.136/2022 for the offences punishable U/Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the insurer and 2nd respondent being the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
3. On service of notice, both the respondents have appeared through their respective counsels but not filed written statement.

Whereas during the pendency of the petition respondent No.1 insurance company has filed application U/o 1 rule 10(2) R/w Sec.151 of CPC to delete the insurance company as the policy was not in force on the date of accident and thereafter this court through its considerable order on 14-08-2023 has allowed the application and deleted the respondent No.1 insurance company.
4. Based on the pleadings, following points are framed:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that on 26-09- 2022 at about 6.20 p.m., when the deceased as pedestrian on near Chowdeshwari temple,
Kannamangala main road, Bangalore district at that time driver of the water tanker bearing Regn No.KA-51-A-8675 driven the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased, due to the forced impact deceased suffered multiple injury and died due to the injuries as alleged by them?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?
5. In order to prove the case, the 4th petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 17 documents as per Ex.P1 to 17.
On the other hand, respondents have not lead any rebuttal evidence.
6. Heard the arguments.

7. My findings on the above issues as under:-
Point No.1 ...
Partly in the affirmative, Point No.2 ...
Partly in the affirmative, Point No.3 ...

As per final order For the following:
REASONS 8. Point No.1:

sentences.text: In Issue No.1 burden is on petitioners to prove that on 26-09-2022 at about 6.20 p.m. near Chowdeshwari temple, Kannamangala main road, bangalore district the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of water tanker bearing Reg. No.KA-51-A-8675 by its driver, due to which deceased Narayanappa sustained grievous injuries and died due to the injuries.

9. In this case during the pendency of the trial the injured petitioner was reported to be dead on 14-07-2023 by the petitioner counsel and application U/o 22 rule 4 along with fresh vakalath as IA No.3 was filed for which respondent has not filed any objection and the same came to be allowed by this court as per order dated 15-09-2023 and accordingly by way of amendment the legal heirs of deceased petitioner were brought on record as petitioner No.1(a) to (d).
10.

In order to prove the accident, as well as rash and negligent driving, petitioner No.1(d) got examined himself as PW.1 and has re-iterated the averments of the petition that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending water tanker bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-A-8675 and and got marked Ex.P1 to 8 police documents.
Whereas the respondent No.2 counsel was absent and also no written statement has been filed by respondent No.2 and as there was no representation hence the same has been taken as no cross.
11. I have perused documentary evidence coupled with oral evidence in detail.

As per Ex.P.1- FIR filed at Cr.No.136/2022 of White field traffic police station, clearly shows that on 27-09-2022 there was an accident and in the said accident, deceased Narayanappa who was the pedestrian met with the accident and sustained grievous injuries and police has registered case against the driver of the water tanker bearing Reg. No.KA-51-A-8675 for the offences punishable U/Sec 279 and 337 of IPC.

Whereas documents at Ex.P-1 to 8 & 10 FIR, Complaint, intimation to police, spot mahazar, Sketch,
seizure mahazar, list of assets and IMV report and charge sheet produced by the petitioners clearly discloses that the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending water tanker bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-A-8675 and the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of offending vehicle.
12. Whereas in order to deny the case of petitioner the respondent No.2/owner has not filed any WS and respondent No.1 insurance company was deleted by this court.
13. No doubt in this case the petitioner was reported to be dead during the pendency of the trial but there is no nexus shown before this court to show that the death of the petitioner is due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident for which it can be safely held that the death is not due to the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident.
14.

Hence in view of my discussion, I am of the opinion that, it can be safely held that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving on the part of driver of water tanker bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-A-8675 as such petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in the Affirmative.

15. Point No. 2 :

sentences.text: In this issue burden is on the petitioner to prove that, they are entitle for compensation as prayed.

While answering issue No.1, I have held that on the relevant date, time and place, the accident had occurred due to negligent act of the offending vehicle and as a result the petitioner has sustained injuries.
Now it is to be seen that whether the petitioner is entitle for compensation?
If so for how much and from whom.
16. Whereas injuries causes deprivation to the body which results in losses entitling claimant to claim damages.
Further damages may vary according to the gravity of the injuries and the said damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. Pecuniary and Non-pecuniary damages.
Pecuniary damages are those like medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning and future loss of earning.

Non- pecuniary damages includes for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering,
loss of amenities in life.
17.

In order to prove the case petitioner No.1(d) is examined as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 17 and it is the case of the petitioner that he has sustained injuries in the accident for which he has taken treatment at MTB Orthopaedic & Trauma hospital, Bengalurru.
Whereas he has produced Ex.P.9 wound certificate and discharge summary at Ex.P11.
On perusal of the documents it discloses that he had sustained Intertrochanteric fracture of left femur.
18. The doctor has opined that the injury is grievous in nature.
Due to the injuries as mentioned in the wound certificate, it appears that petitioner might have suffered pain and sufferings.

19. However in this case during the pendency of the matter petitioner was reported to be dead and nothing is brought on record to show the nexus of the death that petitioner has died due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
Hence in view of the same the legal heirs of the petitioner are only entitled for medical expenses incurred by them for the treatment of the petitioner.

20. Petitioner has produced 13 medical bills marked at Ex.P12 for having taken treatment for the accidental injuries which goes to show that he has spent amount towards his medical treatment,
conveyance and other incidental expenses for a total sum of medical bills amounting to Rs.1,25,858/- for which the legal heirs of the petitioner are entitled for compensation of entire medical expenses as per the bills produced at Ex.P12.

Considering the nature of injury and treatment taken by the petitioner, I deem it proper to award global compensation of Rs.1,25,858/-
towards medical expenses.

Hence, I come to the conclusion that in all the petitioner is entitled for compensation of .1,25,858/-
rounded off to Rs.1,26,000/- (Rupees One lakh twenty six thousand only).
21.
INTEREST:
The petitioner is claiming interest @ 9% per annum on the compensation amount.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Narayanappa vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9147099/
5

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Narayanappa vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/ W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.
Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.

22. LIABILITY :-
In this case respondent is the owner of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-A-8675.
After issuance of notice respondent No.1 has appeared through his counsel but not filed objection statements.

23. Hence, on perusal of the oral and documentary evidence by the petitioner, it goes to show that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the water tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-51-A-8675 by the driver.
Hence, respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
24. ISSUE No.3:-
As per discussion, I proceed to pass the following;
O RD E R
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner No.1(a) to 1(d) are entitled for compensation of .1,26,000 /- (Rupees one lakh twenty six thousand Only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation and shall deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the death of petitioner and award is passed only for medical expenses and also compensation amount is meager hence there is no order as to deposit of the said compensation amount.

Further the compensation amount is order to be released in favour of petitioner No.1(a) to (d)
through RTGS/NEFT on proper identification and after collecting copy of bank pass book having photograph of the petitioner No.1(a) to (d) duly attested by the banker and self attested Aadhar card and Pan card of the petitioner.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
